steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: They agreed to throw money our way, Saria.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Your speech was excellent. All those investors were moved by the future that you painted.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: The future... of course.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: I described some byproducts they would be interested in with the kind of language that they speak.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: It was only one short night, but it was far more exhausting than spending a dozen days in the labs.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: It's something we need to power through, for the time being.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Once our funding is settled, you can move into the laboratories whenever you want.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: You know me well. That's the only reason that I'm bearing with all this.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Right, that academic named Ferdinand Clooney is very interested in your proposal too.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: He'll 'build the most fantastic laboratory in all of Terra at Rhine Lab'—That's what he said.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: I welcome him, then.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I looked into his background.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: He feels more like a businessman than an academic to me. He might not understand you.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: No, Saria.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: I never needed anyone to understand me... Actually, I'd say I've already got more than I could ask for, having met you, someone so like-minded.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: Right now, Rhine needs to amass more capable personnel and projects. We have to, if we're going to reach our ultimate goal.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: You're Control. It's your call.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Some of Ferdinand's methods aren't exactly above board. A decent amount of his projects even have some under-the-table dealings with other big corporations or the government.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I'll have a nice chat with him about the rules of the our cooperation going forward.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: You'll help me take care of this, right?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I'm the Director of Defense. That's my job.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: But it will be very risky for you... and Rhine Lab.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: Wait—

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: I just came up with a few new ideas that might even solve some flaws in that theory of mine—Right, what were you going to say just now?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Never mind.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: Thanks for that, Saria.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: It's because you're always here for me that I can focus on my job without worry.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: You never needed anyone to come save you.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: But you came nonetheless.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: That face again... You're angry.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: All those years out there have made you a more emotional person.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: I thought you'd better understand my decision after you took a good look at the reality of the lands outside.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Answer me.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Did you authorize the experiment at Site 359?

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: I'll never lie to you.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: I'm sure you know that better than anyone.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: But you also don't care what's going on over there...

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: You turned a blind eye to what Ferdinand is doing.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Just like you turned a blind eye to Parvis all those years ago.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: Hm? Which experiment are you talking about?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: You don't remember...

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: You never remember any little thing that isn't related to your own research.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: There is only so much that the human brain can process. I have more worthwhile work for mine to focus on.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: Ferdinand's little tricks bought me some time to relax, and it's thanks to him that I can concentrate even better. And think.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: My experiments have seen some major breakthroughs in the last few days. Why don't I tell you about them?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Why you...

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: It's not like you're not interested.

steps.name: Kristen
steps.text: You're just... worried about all those insignificant people and things.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: They were never insignificant.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: You'll never escape the weight of those people and things, Kristen.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: After all, both you and I... and Rhine Lab too, we're all grounded in this land, we've put down roots.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I'm sorry, Dr. {@nickname}.

options: Why are you apologizing all of a sudden?
Changed your mind again?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Don't worry... We're still on the same side.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I won't do anything to you, at least not right now.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: It's just... It's hard to say.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Kristen might not necessarily be on Saria's side.

options: I heard they used to be very good friends.
I heard they had a falling out.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: You don't know what Rhine Lab was like back when it started...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Kristen's radiance brought all kinds of people in, at first, but it was Saria who quietly propped it all up.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: A falling out, huh? They had a huge fight in the Control office, and blew a huge hole in the roof of the Rhine building. Does that count?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Even then, Saria walked out of the office herself, and Control was completely unscathed too.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: If the two of them... actually played serious, there wouldn't have been anything left standing.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: It's just Kristen doesn't care what kinds of experiments Ferdinand runs.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I was eager to make sure she's okay. That's why I lured you guys here... but I never knew Kristen would interfere with what's going on at the site.

options: That's why it was so important for Ptilopsis to see the truth behind the site herself.
Please inform Ms. Wright
Control needs to know we 'saw' everything.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: You... you're not going to stop at telling Kristen the situation over there?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: The important thing is that you... that Rhodes Island has caught wind of this.

options: If Ms. Wright doesn't want this information, there are lots of people that do.
Like Beachbrella and all the other companies competing with Rhine.
Like the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Arts Units, and Originium.
Like the Maylander Foundation.
Information is the most valuable bargaining chip there is.
Having information is the best way to keep yourself safe.
As long as Ms. Wright wants to keep Rhine Lab alive.
She has to intervene at the site.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: You've been planning to force her hand since before you got here...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Dr. {@nickname}, she might just remember you for this.

options: Good. We really should get to know each other to improve our cooperation.
Sounds like I should be honored.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: You're confident... No, you have real faith in your operators at the site.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: That's wonderful.

options: I have one last question, Director Muelsyse.
Are you bothered by those experiments?
Are you bothered by anything in particular?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Dr. {@nickname}... At the end of the day, I'm the Director of Rhine Lab's Ecological Section. Not a lot of people ask me questions like that to my face.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Hm... How should I answer this...?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Wouldn't you agree that if I didn't keep a secret or two, my charm would take a hit?

steps.name: Mechanist
steps.text: Doctor?

steps.name: Mechanist
steps.text: I still haven't received Ptilopsis's synchronized message.

steps.name: Mechanist
steps.text: Sorry, I don't have the time to fill you in on the details...

steps.name: Mechanist
steps.text: I still have ten... No, maybe eleven hollows to take care of.

steps.name: Mechanist
steps.text: Right, one more thing.

steps.name: Mechanist
steps.text: Ho'olheyak got away.

steps.name: Mechanist
steps.text: She might head to the site... she seemed like she had her own objective.

steps.name: Mechanist
steps.text: Right, I agree with you.

steps.name: Mechanist
steps.text: She's more dangerous than we expected.

steps.name: Mechanist
steps.text: *cough*... How am I doing?

steps.name: Mechanist
steps.text: My robotic arm is overheating a little. That's all.

steps.name: Mechanist
steps.text: I won't let myself get hurt before things really get hairy.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Elena, you're staying here with me.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: You've contributed a lot to the experiment, and I am proud of your results. You've earned the right to stand by my side and witness the glory it brings us.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: You turned the whole site... into a petri dish. You put all those Pioneers in danger just to create that giant monster.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: What could it bring, if not disaster?!

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: The way I see it...?
Several miles out, the silver geometric body remains steadily suspended above the site.
The body seems as if it has started a storm. However, aside from the chaotic gales, there are also countless scraps blowing around it.
Some of the scraps were originally trees, while others were once parts of buildings and machines, but all of them have taken similar shapes, hovering around the body in the center.
The geometric body could appear at any moment on the outskirts of other Columbian cities. It could also suddenly descend upon Londinium or central Kawalerielki.
It has redefined what people imagine when they think of Originium Arts, it has redefined the known rules of physics, and it will soon redefine the already changing tides.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: A new era.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: What I see is a new era. Its arrival carries with it all sorts of possibilities, chances at things we may never have thought possible. It also implies a change in the standings of factions old and new.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: I'm taking these risks not for myself.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: It doesn't necessarily have to be Columbia that enters this new era. It doesn't have to be Rhine, either.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: But when the time comes, our money and connections will both leave us behind.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: The city of steel we have forged will be torn apart at the hands of other nations, just as Lingones became fodder to a new hegemon.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: The laboratories of which we're so proud will be dismantled and sold for scrap on the second-hand market, while Rhine's signs will be forgotten and slowly rust away in an underground warehouse.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: When that time comes, we will lose any chance we ever had to drive change. Our ideals will shatter, and we will be left to live out the rest of our meaningless days staring at the backs of those who have gone ahead.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: When the epoch decides who to leave in the dust, it doesn't think back on past glory, much less hold out for future potential.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: All we can ever seize is the present.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Searching for signal...

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Connection failed.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Still no comms...

steps.name: Greyy
steps.text: Doctor, we've been surrounded.

steps.name: Greyy
steps.text: The living quarters probably won't last long. Soon, this building we end up leveled like the others at the site.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: The silver construct is controlled by the subconsciousness of the Hub's test subjects.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: If we forcibly remove the treatment bands the pioneers are wearing...

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Negative.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Removal of the treatment bands carries as much risk as the removal of Device #9.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: What if we interfere with their neural activities externally?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: No, that's too risky too. It's likely to cause brain damage.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Even without the silver constructs... I have no idea how to go about waking them up. Those who are connected to the system might never wake up again.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: It's my fault... Ferdinand and I were the ones put them in this danger.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: I need to save them. I must...

steps.name: Greyy
steps.text: In thirty seconds, we'll face... the tenth wave of attacks!

steps.name: Greyy
steps.text: No, the frequency is getting faster.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: This can't continue.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: Only I... can stop it.
Tiny grains of sand cloud the air, like an entire house shrouded within a fortress formed of loose sand.
There are countless silver substances laying outside of it. They seem curious about this fortress, not understanding why they cannot dissolve this seemingly fragile barrier.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You didn't stop it...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You're just using your Originium Arts to offset its corrosion.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: And your Arts Unit will fail soon.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: Not yet... Not so fast.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: What have you done to yourself...?

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: Just... a small experiment.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You... You implanted one in yourself...

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: Arts Unit...

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: Before I let anyone else into the lab... I need to ensure of the safety of the requisite steps.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: They're switching up their attack patterns.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: It's part of us. It's curious, and it's a good learner.
A barrage of impact noises can be heard from the outside, as though a storm of silver rain is raging.
The rain keeps opening up holes in the sand wall, which are in turn patched by more sand.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: We need to find some other way to buy time.

steps.name: Greyy
steps.text: Doctor, let me try.

steps.name: Greyy
steps.text: I'll go outside and use my Arts to lure some—

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Greyy, that's too risky!

steps.name: Greyy
steps.text: Doctor, I told Mr. Sonny something when we were chatting earlier—these words have stayed with me for all these years.

steps.name: Greyy
steps.text: If I don't take a step forward, how will I ever know if my path lies out there?

steps.name: Greyy
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Greyy
steps.text: Truth be told... I don't know if I'll be able to do it.

steps.name: Greyy
steps.text: I might even mess up the moment I step outside... I... I can't help but doubt myself...

steps.name: Greyy
steps.text: But what if it works?

steps.name: Greyy
steps.text: All my mentors have taught me that whenever I start doubting myself, I should just remember... I've succeeded before!
He takes a deep breath, lifts his head up, and looks at the darkness in front of him.
The silver geometric body has what appears to be eyes, but he knows what it is that he's looking at.
It's not a new kind of intelligent being, nor is it some kind of mysterious monster.
That is the fruit of human technology. It can be used, analyzed—
And, no doubt, defeated.

steps.name: Greyy
steps.text: You... aren't anything to be afraid of.

steps.name: Greyy
steps.text: Fear always stems from the unknown.

steps.name: Greyy
steps.text: And you... You were created with Arts. You're a byproduct born in the Pioneers' minds.

steps.name: Greyy
steps.text: Humanity triumphed over the darkness of night... How could we lose to our own creations?
A ray of light emits from his hand and bolts toward the dark shadow floating above their heads.
As expected, a not insignificant amount of silver liquid exits out of the Pioneers' quarters and entangles itself with the dark night as it tears madly toward the light he released.
That moment, the light is shredded into pieces, leaving only a few strands progressing deeper into the darkness.
But more and more lights then rise one after another.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: Greyy's a brave man.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: He's just like Sonny... and the pioneers. He has the courage to face his challenges head on.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Its attacks have gotten stronger again...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: All my light can do is distract it; it still sees us as its target.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: *cough*... *cough* *cough*...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Your nose is bleeding...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Even if you have no infected organs, your body's blood vessels won't be able to withstand releasing this much energy... It won't take long for you to hemorrhage to death.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: I... I must protect them, and I'm willing to...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You're willing to give your life.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: That's not an excuse you're using to win over the Pioneers.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You're... really going to do it.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: Dr. Silence, wouldn't you make the same choice to protect your family?

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: I made the wrong decision once.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: And I won't... make the same mistake again.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You mean, your mother...?

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: All these years, I've wondered over and over...

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: How did they feel before they were swallowed whole by the sandstorm?

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: Did they wait, despairing in a cramped space until the moment of death arrived, like these Pioneers?
What if I didn't accept that invitation? Would I have stayed with my mother until the very end?
If she had the qualifications to enter the city with me, would that have spared her from the storm?
My research has solved many difficult problems that were unsolvable, but I still haven't found an answer to this one—
Why was I the only one spared?

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: Dr. Silence...

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: If... If that is really the assemblage of the test subjects' consciousnesses...

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: I love it, just as I loved my family.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: But why... why can't I hear it speak to me?
A deep fissure appears in the sand wall.
Dorothy stumbles forward, but a pair of hands catches her.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Dorothy... No matter how much work you put in, you can't change your mother's fate.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: That storm is in the past... it ended long ago.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: Is... that so?
A drone fills the opening in the sand wall with its own body.
Seemingly injected with life once again, the grains of sand quickly rearrange in an orderly way.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Dorothy, you want to hear your family's voices, right?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You should ask those test subjects.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Once the storm is over, they will tell you their answer.

steps.name: Greyy
steps.text: Agh...
His hand is getting warmer and warmer. He knows that the machinery has been pushed past its limits for so long it is doomed to break.
But he cannot give up.
If he falls here, the island behind him will forever be swallowed whole by the darkness.
He has to hold on, just like that one night all those years ago. He ran so far away, even though his hands had gone numb from the cold and his legs hurt from the long journey—
He needs to make it to that day when he passes the torch he holds to another pair of hands.
Suddenly, a warm power shrouds his hand and helps him stabilize his energy output.
It is someone else's Arts.

steps.name: Greyy
steps.text: O-Operator Ptilopsis...?

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: You require assistance, Operator Greyy.

steps.name: Greyy
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: You needn't alert me to the danger here.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: I had already calculated the probability of our mission's success before I submitted my leave request to Dr. Silence.

steps.name: Greyy
steps.text: What's the number...?

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: With my support as a newly added variable, the probability of our success is...

steps.name: Greyy
steps.text: No, you don't have to tell me.

steps.name: Greyy
steps.text: I'm just used to planning everything out before the actual execution. I know it was hasty of me to run out here, but I couldn't control myself.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Calculating the results will not reveal anything in advance.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Operator Greyy, what determines the result in the end will always be...

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: The 'impulse' that drives you forward.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: I cannot confirm whether the fluctuations of my brainwaves right now were caused by this 'impulse,' but it was none other than your actions that drove me here.

steps.name: Greyy
steps.text: Operator Ptilopsis...

steps.name: Greyy
steps.text: Thanks.
Even more light begins to emanate above him.
This is beyond the theoretical maximum output numbers that he and Mechanist, the designers of the weapon, had yet to measure.
But these are his Arts.
There has never been a theory capable of fully explaining Originium Arts... And furthermore, this luminance comes not only from his Arts Unit... It comes from his heart.
This luminance in the end pierces through the out-of-control test subject, through the darkness, the clouds, and all the unknowns above.
This thought, hidden within the sparks of electricity, pulses once only.
Nonetheless, Greyy grasps hold of it—He can feel the possibility within.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: A weak signal has been detected...

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Connecting.

steps.name: Greyy
steps.text: Phew...
Following an intense quake, the enormous test subject positions itself in front of the assembled onlookers.
There was no foreshadowing, and it left no trails of its movement. It simply appeared in that very position.

steps.name: Greyy
steps.text: Agh...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Stand back, Greyy!

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: That's an order—
Silence grabs Greyy's other hand.
A drone takes to the sky and, gathering the golden rays that began to disperse as Greyy's strength starts to give, charges straight toward the silver colossus that shrouds the sky.
The explosion is as loud as a thunderclap. The drone, having risen to the highest point in the sky, disintegrates into countless specks of light that flutter down.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I picked this up from Elena.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Though a trick like this will only work once.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: This light... will extinguish eventually.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Message sent.

steps.name: Greyy
steps.text: Our most crucial objective has been completed, right?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Yes...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: We did it.
She reaches her other hand out to hold Ptilopsis.
The light above them slowly dissipates, revealing the enormous scale of the silver construct.
Yet it does not advance.
A layer of fine dust still stubbornly stands between them.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Dorothy...?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You're holding... a treatment band and the reagent.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You're thinking of plugging yourself in...

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: I want to hear their voices.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: No!

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I told you. I don't know how to wake them up, and I won't know how to wake you up!

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You might find yourself swallowed by their consciousness, and your nervous system might see irreversible damage if we destroy this construct, and perhaps...

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: I'm a researcher. I'm willing to accept all the uncertainties.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But I'm your doctor!

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I can't just watch you risk your own life—

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: It'll be fine, Olivia.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: This way, I will get to be with my family.
The test subjects behind her are unable to speak.
The silver construct before her remains silent as ever.
Dorothy closes her eyes and feels the silver reagent flow into her body.
The slightly cold sensation feels as if the fingertips of her family members are caressing her up and down.

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: Olivia...

steps.name: Dorothy
steps.text: I need the answer.
